entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ashina Yuanqing was a puppet Turkic khagan installed by Wu Zetian in 685. He ruled over the Turkic khaganate during a time of great instability and fragmentation, as various Turkic tribes and Chinese dynasties vied for power. Ashina Yuanqing's significance lies in his role as a tool for Wu Zetian, who sought to expand Chinese influence in Central Asia. He also played a part in the development of the Tibetan Empire, which would go on to become a major power in the region. Despite his relatively short tenure, Ashina Yuanqing left a lasting legacy in the history of the Silk Road and the development of Tibetan Buddhism.

Ashina Yuanqing was born into a prominent Turkic family and was likely educated in traditional Turkic and Buddhist scholars. He was appointed as the khagan in 685, following the death of his predecessor, Bao Xian. Wu Zetian, who had recently ascended to the throne of the Tang Dynasty, saw an opportunity to expand Chinese influence in Central Asia and installed Ashina Yuanqing as her puppet ruler. He was given significant autonomy to govern the Turkic khaganate, but was ultimately answerable to Wu Zetian.

Ashina Yuanqing's rule was marked by a series of military campaigns against neighboring tribes and the Tibetan Empire. He also oversaw the development of a number of important trade routes, including the Silk Road, which connected China with Central Asia and Europe. Despite his efforts to expand Chinese influence, Ashina Yuanqing's rule was ultimately cut short by the Tibetan Empire, which defeated his forces in a series of battles. He was killed in 693 CE, marking the end of his relatively short but significant reign.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ashina Yuanqing played a significant role in the development of the Silk Road and the spread of Tibetan Buddhism during his reign. His legacy continues to be felt in the region, and he is remembered as a key figure in the history of Central Asia.
